content:
Maya (PMM): Quick thread 4 so we can finalize the battlecard + SDR snippets for the webinar funnel. Need: 3 rebuttals per competitor bucket (cloud AI platforms / generic LLM APIs / infra vendors), 2 inbound routing rules, and a short benchmark blurb we can include on the landing. Deadline: Thursday EOD.
Jon (Growth): Ill own SDR snippets + tracking. Will also drop suggested HubSpot properties and webhook tags.
Keisha (AE): Ill paste common buyer lines we hear from platform teams vs product teams. Real quotes help.
Ravi (Bench): I have fresh micro-benchmarks from last week. Note: we should avoid named-cloud %-claims. I can give ranges and a cost-per-1k-token ballpark.
Sam (Designer): I'll make a compact slide for the webinar and a hero image variant for A/B. Need headline options.
Maya (PMM): Rebuttal structure: 1-line claim, 1-line evidence (directional), 1-action for rep. Keep it tiny.
Keisha (AE): For cloud platforms:
- Claim: "We already run everything on CloudX."
- Rebuttal: "Reserved pools + SLA-backed routing for production-critical flows vs best-effort burst instances."
- Rep action: "Ask: Do you run mission-critical routes on on-demand spots or reserved capacity?"
Keisha (AE): For generic LLM APIs:
- Claim: "We just call a hosted API, simpler."
- Rebuttal: "Unified runtime + observability + model rollouts reduce ops overhead vs glueing inference and tracing tools."
- Rep action: "Offer: 15-min technical review to show trace + cost breakdown."
Keisha (AE): For infra vendors/self-host stacks:
- Claim: "We'll build our own stack, cheaper long term."
- Rebuttal: "Upfront infra + reliability tax + missing eval tooling often makes total cost higher; we provide turnkey observability and rollouts."
- Rep action: "Ask about current ops headcount/time spent on tuning and rollouts."
Ravi (Bench): Micro-bench blurb (safe wording): "In our internal tests on commonly used transformer configs, typical median per-token latencies for small sequence workloads fall in the ~1560ms range depending on model/quantization; configuration and batching materially change tail latency. We recommend dedicated pools for production-critical routes."
legal-bot: Heads up  external comparisons and latency ranges should be reviewed by Legal before public use. See policy: https://confluence.example/legal/bench-claims.
Maya (PMM): Good — we'll tag the copy "legal-review" and hold publishing until signoff. Keep numbers as ranges.
Jon (Growth): Inbound routing rules (HubSpot props + server webhook tags):
```yaml
hubspot_properties:
  - name: company_size
    values: enterprise, midmarket, startup
  - name: inference_priority
    values: production, experiment
webhook_tags:
  - bench_conscious
  - high_token_trial
  - requires_sales_demo
```
Jon (Growth): Map: enterprise + production -> route to AE queue (urgent). Trial + high_token_trial -> Growth SDR nurture + engineering touch. Low-usage self-serve -> automated onboarding.
Sam (Designer): Headline options for landing page:
- "Serve LLMs at production scale  predictable latency, predictable cost."
- "Ship reliable LLM features without rebuilding your infra."
- "Lower token cost, not your SLAs."
Maya (PMM): Pick two for A/B. Also need 2x 30s social copy variants and a speaker blurb.
Jon (Growth): SDR snippets (very short):
- Cold inbound: "Hi NAME  noticed your team calls the OpenAPI a lot. We help guarantee tail latency and cut per-token spend for production routes. Quick chat?"
- Warm inbound: "Hi NAME  congrats on the pilot. We can run a 15-min cost-accuracy check and show where you might save on tokens while keeping latency SLOs."
Keisha (AE): Add objection: "We can't commit to vendor lock" -> Reply: "We support hybrid: same API across hosted/dedicated/private so you can start hosted and export later."
Ravi (Bench): Cost note (directional): "Observed CPU/GPU cost per 1k tokens varies; in sample configs we saw order-of-magnitude differences between naive batching vs workload-aware batching. Use dynamic batching + KV caching for best ROI."
legal-bot: Reminder  no named competitor %s or absolute hardware promises. OK to use ranges and 'we observed' language.
Maya (PMM): Action items:
- @Jon: draft HubSpot mapping + webhook payloads (today)
- @Keisha: paste 5 actual buyer quotes (today)
- @Ravi: finalize blurb and short slide (tomorrow)
- @Sam: do hero variants + slide (tomorrow)
- I'll consolidate into battlecard and send to Legal by Wednesday morning.
Sam (Designer): I'll also export social image sizes.
Keisha (AE): One more quick line for reps to close: "If latency or cost matters, let's run a 2-hour tracer and token burn review."
Maya (PMM): Love it. We'll ship the SDR playbook and the webinar comms after Legal signoff. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
